messages:
josh: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak, we're seeing a 6-8% p50->p99 spike on host-side for short streaming requests (<64B frames). logs show extra syscall path in grpc writev handling.

lina: ugh. can you paste the trace? which change exactly?

josh: it's the kernel affinity fallback from the batcher rewrite (commit 9a7c). here's the hot stack from perf: 
```
#0  sendmsg
#1  writev_grpc -> grpc_stream_writev
#2  streaming_coalesce -> parse_frame_gather
#3  host_preparse -> tokenize_small
#4  request_handler
```

ben: quick thought — did we regress writev coalescing thresholds? the batcher now prefers kernel path B when seq_len<32 which might cause extra syscalls.

sara: i ran a microbench comparing old vs new selector on same traffic (100k small requests): old p99=12.8ms, new p99=13.7ms. p50 unchanged. so tail affected.

josh: ^exactly. kv-cache hit rate unaffected. looks like extra memcpy + syscall churn. also seeing grpc windowing producing 2x more frames per request.

lina: can we try toggling the batching heuristic to force kernel A for short sequences? bench it.

ben: did that locally — forcing kernel A reduces syscalls and p99 drops back to 12.6ms. but CPU usage slightly higher (2-3%). tradeoff seems worth it for tail-sensitive workloads.

sara: can we add a transient experiment — canary the selector with a flag per host to route 5% traffic to old strategy and measure tail? perf-bot can do auto-aggregation.

perf-bot: experiment created: "selector-canary-5pct" id=exp-2026-03-22-01

josh: thanks. next steps: (1) run canary overnight, (2) add metric for syscall count per request in ingress, (3) consider hybrid strategy: kernel A for seq<64 or when stream_chunk_count>1.

lina: I'll open PR with a flag and metric. pinging @ben for code review when ready :+1:

ben: on it. will also add test for writev coalesce threshold values.

sara: logging note — add trace tag "kernel_choice" in streaming traces so we can filter quickly in Console.

josh: agreed. will add tag and a dashboard tile for syscall-per-request. thanks team :rocket:
